spec: DESIGN.md — installations, the machine seam, standalone save cards (issue #181)
description: RPCS3's savedata answer where the question names a PS3 game: the title id read from the PARAM.SFO a folder dump or an image boots, or from a PSN package's header (atlas/ps3_title.py), and the savedata folders beginning with it in the one user account's tree stated as the game's save unit, own-folders-by-prefix — or the save_id hole where the id, the account or the folders are not established.

vectors.name: rpcs3-a-folder-dump-names-the-titles-savedata-folders
vectors.rationale: The question names a folder dump: Game.ps3 holds PS3_DISC.SFB and PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN, the fourth boot file RPCS3 searches a directory for (GetElfPathFromDir, System.cpp:1036-1063 at build d5213de6), and Emulator::Load reads TITLE_ID from PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO (System.cpp:1713-1745; get_sfo_dir_from_game_path, system_utils.cpp:516-566) — here BLUS30443. One user account, 00000001, holds a localusername, so its savedata is the one the game writes. There the game's folders are BLUS30443GAMEDATA and BLUS30443-AUTOSAVE — a game names its folders and RPCS3 lists its own by the title id it runs (cellSaveData.cpp:228-249, :312-314, :822-826). BLES00001SAVE is another game's and is left out, BLUS30443.txt is no folder, and .backup_BLUS30443GAMEDATA is the utility's own scratch copy (:1500-1502), which begins with a period, not the id. The group carries own-folders-by-prefix with prefix BLUS30443, needs is empty, and ps3-save-prefix-may-differ says the game, not the emulator, picked the prefix.

vectors.name: rpcs3-a-dumps-boot-file-names-the-same-title
vectors.rationale: The question names the dump's PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN itself, an executable: its title id is the PARAM.SFO RPCS3 loads for it, in the directory above the executable's own — PS3_GAME, which holds no PS3_DISC.SFB, so its own PARAM.SFO (System.cpp:1738-1739; get_sfo_dir_from_game_path, system_utils.cpp:516-566). The answer is the folder dump's: the same unit.

vectors.name: rpcs3-a-psn-package-names-its-title-from-its-header
vectors.rationale: The question names a PSN package. Its header is unencrypted, and RPCS3 installs it under the nine bytes at offset 55 — the title part of the content id UP0006-NPUB30058_00-… (read_metadata, Crypto/unpkg.cpp:249-253; PKGHeader, unpkg.h:103-119). That id names the folder NPUB30058SAVE01 in the one account's savedata, and the unit says so.

vectors.name: rpcs3-two-user-accounts-state-no-unit
vectors.rationale: The title id reads, and two accounts hold a localusername. Which one the emulator runs is a runtime selection no file records (Emulator::m_usr, System.h:108), so a restore must not guess it: both trees stay groups, neither carries a unit, and the title id stays the save_id hole, its fill spelled ps3-title-id.
